question.value: Determine the polarization and Faraday rotation structure of the nucleus (multiple polarized components versus internal Faraday rotation) and the magnetic field structure of the kiloparsec-scale jet in the quasar 3C 273 using multiband ALMA polarimetry.

evidence.quote: We used multiband Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) data to study the polarization structure of both the nucleus and the kiloparsec-scale jet of the archetypal quasar 3C 273.

The broad wavelength coverage (145–345 GHz) allows us to revisit the extreme Faraday rotation previously detected in band 6 alone and to better test whether the behavior arises from multiple polarized components or from internal Faraday rotation within the nuclear region.

findings_qualitative.value: In the kiloparsec-scale jet, the magnetic field is predominantly poloidal along the jet until ~2'' from hotspot H2, where it turns perpendicular in the inner jet (transverse shock) and parallel/circumferential along the jet edges (shearing).

evidence.quote: The magnetic field direction is predominantly poloidal along the jet direction until about $2\ensuremath{''}$ from the brightest hotspot H2. Closer to the hotspot, the magnetic field in the inner jet is perpendicular to the jet, while around the edges the magnetic field follows the jet direction.

claims.hypothesis: The extreme Faraday rotation and inverse depolarization in the nucleus of 3C 273 arise either from multiple polarized components or from a single component undergoing internal Faraday rotation.
claims.experiment: Perform Bayesian QU-fitting of complex fractional polarization across ALMA Bands 4, 6, and 7 (138-350 GHz) comparing single thin (S), single internal/inverse-depolarization (T_inv), double thin (S2), and double external-dispersion (T2) models.
claims.result: Model T2 achieves the highest Bayesian evidence (ln Z = 6437, chi^2_r = 0.35), decisively ruling out S2 (Delta ln Z = 141), T_inv (Delta ln Z = 1155), and S (Delta ln Z = 4302), yielding RM_1 = +(2.58 +- 0.08) x 10^5 rad m^-2 and RM_2 = +(1.48 +- 0.18) x 10^4 rad m^-2.
claims.finding: The nuclear millimeter polarization of 3C 273 is governed by a multicomponent Faraday structure rather than a single internal Faraday-rotating component.

evidence.quote: Table 2 shows that among the four tested models, the two–component external–dispersion case (T2) provides the highest Bayesian evidence and the lowest reduced $\chi^2$.

evidence.loc: Polarization and Faraday rotation in the core
evidence.quote: With the much smaller wavelength coverage of those single-band observations, we were unable to distinguish between the two models unlike here where the single inverse depolarization model (T~inv~) corresponding to the internal Faraday rotation model of is clearly disfavored.

claims.hypothesis: The Faraday screen and polarized emission in the nucleus of 3C 273 are time-variable and linked to the beamed parsec-scale jet.
claims.experiment: Compare Band 7 nuclear EVPAs between two executions separated by 8 days (15 and 23 November 2018) and compare Band 6 EVPAs with 2016-2017 ALMA observations.
claims.result: A 10 deg EVPA jump is observed in Band 7 over 8 days (confirmed by AMAPOLA), and the nominal Band 6 RM changed from ~5.0 x 10^5 and ~2.5 x 10^5 rad m^-2 in prior epochs to ~-8.4 x 10^4 rad m^-2 in November 2018.
claims.finding: The nuclear polarization and Faraday rotation vary on timescales of a week to 1.5 years, linking the millimeter core polarization to dynamic components in the beamed parsec-scale jet.

evidence.quote: However, a $10\deg$ shift in the EVPAs of the nucleus was found, showing evidence of an intrinsic EVPA variability of the nucleus.
We detect variability in the polarization angle on timescales of a week, which further suggests that the emission of the nucleus is connected with the parsec-scale beamed jet.

claims.hypothesis: Millimeter-wavelength synchrotron emission in the kiloparsec-scale jet and hotspot region traces the same electron population and magnetic field topology as centimeter-wavelength emission.
claims.experiment: Image Stokes I, Q, U and spectral index (138-350 GHz) across the kiloparsec-scale jet in Bands 4, 6, and 7 and extract longitudinal ridge and transverse hotspot profiles.
claims.result: Hotspot H2 shows 20-30% fractional polarization, ridge spectral index is ~-0.9 to -0.8 steepening at H2, and the magnetic field is parallel to the jet up to 2'' before H2, perpendicular at the H2 shock, and parallel along the jet edges.
claims.finding: The millimeter polarization and spectral index structures closely match centimeter VLA observations, indicating a common synchrotron-emitting electron population experiencing shock compression at H2 and velocity shear at the jet boundary.

evidence.quote: Overall, the variations we observe along the ridge line look very similar to those at centimeter wavelengths (cite: conway93), suggesting that the same population of synchrotron-emitting electrons is also responsible for the millimeter-wavelength emission.
The magnetic field direction in the hotspot region follows the jet edges, which can result from the shearing of an originally tangled magnetic field (cite: laing80).

why_this_data.value: Multiband ALMA observations (Bands 4, 6, 7) provide broad wavelength-squared coverage to break model degeneracies from single-band observations, and separate pointings on the nucleus and hotspot H2 keep the kiloparsec-scale jet within the inner third of the primary beam where polarization calibration is reliable.

evidence.quote: Due to the limited wavelength coverage of our observations, we were unable to discriminate between the two scenarios. Additionally, because the ALMA polarization calibration could be performed reliably only for the inner third of the primary beam of the telescopes, we were unable to study the polarization structure of the kiloparsec-scale jet.

Because we were interested in the polarization of both the nucleus and kiloparsec-scale jet, we performed two separate pointings in each band: one centered on the nucleus (3C 273) and another on the bright hotspot H2 (3C273_H2) about 21.3$''$ away.

why_this_method.value: Complex-plane QU-fitting with nested sampling avoids EVPA n-pi ambiguity and allows rigorous Bayesian evidence comparison across multi-component models; Monte Carlo visibility fitting accounts for systematic D-term and bandpass uncertainties.

evidence.loc: Extracting Stokes parameters of the nucleus
evidence.quote: Following , we ran Monte Carlo (MC) simulations to account for thermal and systematic uncertainties in the data, and obtained a distribution of 1000 Stokes I, Q, U, and V values.

We performed this QU-fitting in the complex plane using parametric models, $p(\lambda^2;\,\bm{\theta})$, and a nested-sampling backend that returns posterior samples for the parameter set $\bm{\theta}$ and the Bayesian evidence $\ln\mathcal{Z}$ for model comparison.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single Faraday-thin component (model S), single inverse-depolarizing component (model T_inv), and two Faraday-thin components (model S2) for the core polarization — all decisively ruled out by Bayesian evidence.

evidence.quote: The simpler two–thin component model (S2) gives an inferior but acceptable fit based on the reduced $\chi^2$ but is decisively ruled out based on the Bayes Factor ($\Delta\ln\mathcal{Z}\simeq140$).
The single–component models (T~inv~, S) cannot reproduce the observed fractional polarization or EVPA behavior and are also decisively disfavored.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using the 23 November 2018 Band 7 execution for core modeling — rejected due to a 10 deg EVPA jump and poor spectral index continuity (reduced chi^2 = 123.0 vs 2.76 for 15 November).

evidence.loc: Extracting Stokes parameters of the nucleus
evidence.quote: If we use the 23 November epoch instead, the spectral index would be $-0.905\pm0.002$ with a significantly higher reduced $\chi^2=123.0$, further supporting our decision to use only the 15 November epoch in the modeling of the core polarization.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Log-parabola curved spectral fit in the kiloparsec-scale jet — rejected because BIC does not disfavor the simpler power-law fit.

evidence.loc: Polarization and spectral index of the kiloparsec-scale jet
evidence.quote: We found that a log-parabola shape results in a smaller reduced $\chi^2$; however, according to the Bayesian information criterion (BIC), we cannot disfavor the simpler power-law fit.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Stopped at the two-component external-dispersion model (T2) because it achieved reduced chi^2 = 0.35 and decisive Bayes factors over alternatives, while non-simultaneity across bands and lack of contemporaneous VLBI priors make more complex models unwarranted.

evidence.quote: Therefore, we do not consider it useful to fit more complicated models (or equally complicated models with different underlying assumptions) in the absence of more robust prior information based on contemporaneous very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) imaging.

limitations_admitted.value: Core emission is spatially unresolved by ALMA (~2 kpc scale), making it impossible to distinguish external Faraday dispersion from internal Faraday rotation within the two components.

evidence.quote: While the best-fit-model equation is nominally of external Faraday rotation, we note that in the case of unresolved emission we cannot reliably distinguish this from internal Faraday rotation effects that would cause similar spectro-polarimetric behavior.

limitations_admitted.value: Observations across Bands 4, 6, and 7 were spread over a week (11-18 November 2018), introducing systematic uncertainty in the multi-band core modeling due to potential source variability.

evidence.quote: We also note that as the data in the different bands are not strictly simultaneous, and we see significant variability in the band 7 EVPA on a timescale of a week, there is additional uncertainty in the best-fit model due to potential variability.

limitations_admitted.value: Five antennas present on 15 November 2018 in Band 7 were absent on 23 November 2018 and therefore could not be corrected for instrumental polarization (D-terms).

evidence.quote: There are, however, five antennas that were present on 15 November and were not available on 23 November. For those antennas, we did not correct for instrumental polarization.

limitations_admitted.value: Sensitivity and wavelength-squared coverage in the kiloparsec-scale jet are insufficient to detect the small (~2 rad m^-2) Faraday rotation or to map transverse polarization in X-ray bright knots A and B.

evidence.quote: We attempted to make an RM map of the kiloparsec-scale jet by using the data of the individual Spws similar to the spectral index map, but due to the relatively poor sensitivity and larger EVPA uncertainties, we do not detect any RM deviating from 0 rad m$^−2$ within three times the RM uncertainty.

In this model, the very-high-energy gamma-ray emission would originate in the brightest X-ray knots, A and B, but unfortunately the sensitivity of our polarization maps is not high enough to detect polarization across the jet in this region to study if it supports the scenario of a sheared layer around the jet, as seen in the hotspot region.

referee_caveats_inferred: The reduced chi^2 of 0.35 for the best-fit T2 model indicates that the channel-wise Monte Carlo error bars (which include inflated systematic D-term noise) are likely overestimated or correlated across channels within a spectral window.

Because the two components in the T2 model are fit to total fractional polarization q and u without spectral index parameters for each polarized component, any intrinsic spectral index difference between the two emission regions is absorbed into the effective Faraday dispersion parameters sigma_RM.

data_public_as_stated.value: Raw ALMA data ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00357.S stated; extracted channel-wise core polarization table (poldata.dat) and Stokes I, Q, U FITS maps of the kiloparsec-scale jet publicly available at CDS.

evidence.quote: The polarization data used in the QU-modeling are available as a table poldata.dat in electronic form at the CDS via <http://cdsweb.u-strasbg.fr/cgi-bin/qcat?J/A+A/>.
The Stokes I, Q, and U maps of the outer kiloparsec-scale jet are available in fits format at the CDS.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00357.S.

products_in_archive.value: QA2 images delivered with the dataset mentioned; final Stokes I, Q, U FITS maps and core polarization table hosted at CDS.

evidence.loc: Imaging and alignment of the kiloparsec-scale jet
evidence.quote: Because the self-cal we applied changed the absolute position of the phase center in our images, we used the quality assurance level 2 (QA2) images delivered within the dataset (with no self-cal applied) to verify the image alignment between different bands.
The Stokes I, Q, and U maps of the outer kiloparsec-scale jet are available in fits format at the CDS.

missing_for_reproduction: Prior bounds and specific nested sampling algorithm/package used for QU-fitting
Custom Monte Carlo CASA script used to perturb calibration tables and compute parallactic angle
Exact tclean weighting (e.g., Briggs robust parameter), cell sizes for Bands 4 and 7, and stopping criteria
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~50-150 GB of raw visibilities (four full-polarization 12-m executions across Bands 4, 6, and 7 with 256 total channels); <100 MB for the CDS table and FITS images.
reproducibility.score_reason: High reproducibility: raw ALMA data are public, the intermediate channel-by-channel Stokes table (poldata.dat) and FITS images are deposited at CDS, the calibration overrides (flux scales, self-cal intervals, Band 6 self-bandpass model, MC noise amplitudes) and QU-fitting analytic equations are explicitly given. Minor deductions for omitting the nested-sampling priors/software name and tclean weighting parameters.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Both raw ALMA visibilities (2018.1.00357.S) and the intermediate extracted core polarization spectrum (poldata.dat at CDS) are public, and the main results are exact numeric Bayesian QU-fitting parameters (RM, sigma_RM, p_0, psi_0, ln Z) and core spectral index.

methods_papers.why: Spw-independent polarization calibrator modeling to mitigate D-term spectral slopes
Self-bandpass calibration, UVMULTIFIT visibility extraction, and Monte Carlo polarization error estimation procedure
UVMULTIFIT library for visibility-domain component fitting
QU-fitting formalism for Faraday rotation modeling

companion_papers.why: Previous single-band (ALMA Band 6) polarimetry of the 3C 273 nucleus that motivated this multiband follow-up
